successors.name: British South Africa Company
successors.text: Matabeleland and the Midlands: 'The kingdom was located between the Sanyati and Limpopo rivers'; the Rozvi state was 'conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele'

ledger.x: c. 1823: Mzilikazi leaves Nguniland with Shaka's cattle and founds his own kingdom. 'In 1823 Mzilikazi left Nguniland during the Mfecane with a large kraal of Shaka's cattle.' Infobox: 'Reign: c. 1823-1868'.
1826: the Ndebele move into the Transvaal.
1836-37: Voortrekkers arrive and fight the Ndebele in the Transvaal.

1838: Mzilikazi 'withdrew from the Marico Valley with his regiments and loyalists'; the Mzilikazi page: 'By early 1838, Mzilikazi and his people were forced northwards and out of Transvaal altogether'.
early 1838: the Ndebele are driven out of the Transvaal.

c. 1838: the Ndebele conquer the Rozvi state. 'it was invaded by no less than six groups which had fled during the Mfecane ... until it was conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele'; the Ndebele 'reached the upper Mzingwane Valley (next to the Rozvi state) in 1839 where they settled'.
1840: Mzilikazi settles in Matabeleland with his Ndiweni and Nkulumane followers.
1847: Boer attacks on the Ndebele Limpopo frontier begin.
1852: the Ndebele make peace with the Boers.
October 1893: the First Matabele War begins.
January 1894: Lobengula dies and the war ends.
January 1894: the Ndebele kingdom ends with the death of its last king Lobengula ('second and last king (1870-94) of the Mthwakazi (Matabele) nation'), after Bulawayo fell on 3 November 1893.

wars.name: Ndebele wars with the Voortrekkers
wars.outcome: The Voortrekkers lost the first battle; in 1837 they 'destroyed eGabeni and other Matabele camps along the Marico River' in a nine-day battle, and Mzilikazi withdrew north by early 1838.

wars.name: Ndebele conquest of the Rozvi
wars.outcome: The Rozvi state was 'conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele'; the Ndebele settled the Mzingwane valley in 1839 and Matabeleland in 1840.

wars.name: Ndebele-Boer border war on the Limpopo
wars.outcome: 'campaigns defending the Limpopo line in battles against the Boer attacks of 1847-1851', ended by a peace treaty in 1852; no border change is dated.

wars.name: First Matabele War
wars.outcome: The BSAP columns won at the Shangani (25 October) and Bembesi (1 November); Bulawayo was reached on 3 November 1893; Lobengula fled and died in January 1894; Matabeleland came under Company control.

certainty.note: 'between the Sanyati and Limpopo rivers'; no boundary is described before the 1893-94 conquest.
